 Ed Case and Jill Tokuda win re-election to the U.S. House
 By Dan Nakaso 
 Today 
 • 
 Last updated
 8:45 p.m. 
 Share on Facebook 
 Share on X 
 Share by email 
 -->
 COURTESY PHOTOS
 U.S. Rep. Ed Case and U.S. Rep. Jill Tokuda easily won re-election.
 U.S. Reps. Ed Case and Jill Tokuda easily won re-election today as part of a nationwide blue wave tsunami that will see a return of Democratic control of both the U.S. House and U.S. Senate when the next Congress is sworn this coming January.
 In the first election night results that included all mail-in ballots and early in-person voting, Tokuda received 71% of the votes compared to her Republican challenger, state Sen. Brenton Awa (R, Kaneohe-Laie-Mokuleia), who drew only 29% of votes to represent rural Oahu and all of the neighbor islands.
 Awa’s state Senate seat was not up for election this year, so he was in a safe position to challenge Tokuda and will return to the state Legislature when the next session begins in January.
 And Case swept to victory with 76% of the vote over a field of three challengers to represent urban Honolulu in Congress: Adriel Lam, a Republican; Jordan Conley, of the Green Party; and nonpartisan candidate Nathan Berning.
 Neither of Hawaii’s U.S. Sens. Brian Schatz and Mazie Hirono were up for election today.
 But all four members of Hawaii’s Congressional delegation agreed separately that the priority for Congressional Democrats is bringing down the cost of living — including lowering the cost of everything from fuel to healthcare to groceries — while holding President Donald Trump’s administration accountable as a co-equal branch of government that’s been lacking under Republican control of both the House and Senate.

 Tokuda said that House Democrats already have plans to address the economy in the first “100 hours” — not 100 days — after the next Congress is sworn in this January.
 They plan to call for a suspension of the federal gas tax, curtail Trump’s on-going tariff war, including with once-friendly nations like Canada, and call on Congress to demand that Trump end his war in Iran and re-open the Straight of Hormuz that has strangled exports of fuel around the world and driven up prices for gas and diesel that have contributed to the increase in nearly all consumer goods.
 Voters today were inspired to turn out because of the economy, Tokuda said.
 But holding the Trump administration accountable is connected to the high cost of living, she said.
 “Long-term real affordability only comes by holding people accountable for the bad decisions that got us to this place,” she said. “When you launch a war on Iran unilaterally, when you tariff our allies who provide our goods and services, this is how life becomes quickly unaffordable.”
 Rep. Case — who serves on two House Appropriation subcommittees with oversight of the Departments of Defense and Homeland Security — said that Democrats have to remember that “Top of mind” for Americans “is the cost of living. That’s what this election was centrally run on.
 ”The voters of the country returned a Democratic majority to Congress because they felt that this current administration and the Republican majority wasn’t addressing that issue,” Case said.
 At the same time, he said, House Democrats need to ensure they fulfill their Constitutional role to act as a “responsible check-and-balance” on Trump, his administration and their policies as a co-equal branch of the federal government.
 In their oversight role as the House majority, Case warned Democrats not to hold hearings that will result in “two years of political theater (or else) we will essentially fall into the same place as the Republicans have been in.”
 Sen. Hirono agreed that Democrats need to address the economy by holding the Trump administration accountable for what it’s done to drive up prices while enriching millionaires and billionaires, in part, by slashing programs like the Affordable Care Act, SNAP food benefits and other programs that help millions of Americans while providing tax benefits for the rich.
 “It’s all on the table,” Hirono said. “I don’t think there’s an either or situation because we have an administration, or a regime as I call it, that has pretty much dismantled all levels of government where you have hundreds of thousands of federal employees either fired or took early retirement.
 “This is a dismantling of government except for the Department of Defense which is getting over a trillion dollars even as they’re dismantling Medicaid, for example,” Hirono said. “So, it’s not an either or choice. We know that people are suffering in terms of affordability issues, including the cost of gasoline, diesel for farmers, fertilizer, housing, healthcare, you name it. As I visit people in Hawaii, businesses, small businesses are being impacted by the tariffs.”
 Sen. Schatz said in a statement to the Honolulu Star-Advertiser that, “Our number one priority is ending the war of choice in Iran that has jacked up gas prices in Hawaii and everywhere else. We’re going to work to reverse the deep cuts this administration has made to SNAP and Medicaid that have made it more expensive for people to get food and health care. And we’re going to hold this out-of-control administration accountable. Democrats are going to work every day to make life more affordable for people, and I hope the results of this election will encourage President Trump and Republicans to work with us.”
